strengths: Well-motivated training-free approach that addresses a real trade-off between computational cost and reasoning coverage, with compelling motivation for soft geometry over hard constraints

Strong and consistent empirical results: up to 13-point AUC improvements across 7 benchmarks (math and code) on Qwen3-8B with only 1.1-1.3× overhead, outperforming both training-free sampling and RL-tuned baselines

Comprehensive experimental analysis including component ablations (Table 3), training stage effects (Figure 5), mode collapse visualization (Figure 4), and cost-robustness frontier analysis (Figure 3)

Sound technical design: tangent-space sampling correctly preserves manifold structure, chunk-wise KV cache resets elegantly maintain linear memory, and fixed random projections keep the method training-free
Clear algorithmic presentation (Algorithm 1) and generally well-written paper with effective visualizations of key concepts
weaknesses: Incomplete paper with critical implementation details missing: multiple unresolved appendix references ('Appendix ??', 'Table ??', 'Figure ??'), projection matrices W, Aℓ, Bℓ not fully specified, and key hyperparameter justifications deferred to unavailable sections, severely impacting reproducibility

Limited technical novelty: latent anchors resemble Delethink, soft regularization is standard, and chunk-based generation is not new; the contribution amounts to an empirical combination of three regularizers lacking principled justification

No theoretical grounding for design choices: why this specific combination of foresight + bumpiness + uniformity? Why is single-sample rollout sufficient for ranking? Bumpiness penalty (Eq. 5) measures within-rollout smoothness, not cross-chunk coherence after KV cache resets. Hyperparameter choices (λb, λu, δ=0.2, r=8) appear ad-hoc

Narrow evaluation scope: primarily Qwen3-8B only, limited to two model families (Qwen3, Phi-4), no evaluation on other major models (Claude, Llama, Gemini), restricted to math/code domains, and no validation on truly long-context benchmarks despite claims about long-context reasoning

Questionable comparison fairness: 'Avg. Tokens' metric conflates generation and rollout tokens across methods, K=8 candidate rollouts per boundary is substantial compute yet unclear if baselines receive matched budgets, RL training costs not directly compared, and no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals

Technical concerns: state extraction using only <EOC> hidden state (Eq. 1) may lose chunk-level information without justification; latency overhead acknowledged but dismissed despite being significant for practical deployment; 'linear memory' claim (Section 3.1) doesn't fully account for context window S=512; hard geometry analysis doesn't rigorously explain why soft penalties specifically help

Limited analysis and missing evidence: Figure 4 (left) uses PCA for visualization without validating it captures semantic diversity; missing Table ?? on latent statistics (Neff); no failure case analysis; interesting observation about smaller gains on RL-optimized models (Figure 5) deserves deeper investigation but receives only passing mention

No code release mentioned and insufficient detail for reproduction: hyperparameter sensitivity only analyzed for K and s (Figure 4 right), initialization of random matrices unspecified, exact sampling configuration unclear despite temperature=0.6 mention, key design choices not ablated

strengths: Rigorous experimental methodology with unified inference budgets, 7 benchmarks, 4 model scales, and comprehensive ablations
Thorough hard-geometry analysis showing exponential acceptance-rate collapse in high dimensions, providing principled motivation for soft regularization
Practical results: 10-13 point AUC gains with only 1.1-1.3× inference overhead, demonstrating strong cost-robustness trade-off
Excellent reproducibility: complete hyperparameters, implementation details in appendices, multiple seeds, and end-to-end token accounting
Insightful analyses of mode collapse (Table 13), training-stage effects on inference-time controllability (Figure 5), and efficiency frontier dominance (Figure 3)
Well-designed technical framework with principled scoring function combining look-ahead utility, trajectory smoothness, and diversity
Comprehensive supplementary material covering theory, failure taxonomy, qualitative cases, and sensitivity analyses
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: combines existing techniques (chunk-based generation, soft regularization, KV resets) rather than introducing fundamental innovations
Oversold 'manifold-informed' framing: soft regularizers don't directly model manifold geometry; connection to differential geometry is loose and largely heuristic

Single Monte Carlo rollout (NMC=1) for foresight value risks noise when candidate scores are close; limited analysis of variance-reduction strategies despite removing V_fore causing largest degradation (-17.8%)
Fixed random matrices (W, A_ℓ, B_ℓ) with only brief sensitivity analysis; unclear robustness across different random initializations
Bounded context truncation (Eq. 18-19) discards history; acknowledged as 'Aggressive KV Reset Loss' failure mode but frequency and magnitude not quantified
Marginal Pass@1 improvements (1-2 points across benchmarks) limit applicability to single-sample use cases; advantage primarily in high-k coverage
Narrow experimental scope: only math and code benchmarks (verification-friendly); pilot open-ended evaluations limited; no evaluation on commonsense, multi-hop, or reading comprehension reasoning
Inference overhead of 1.1-1.3× is non-trivial for latency-sensitive serving; vague mitigation strategies ('selective search') without systematic study
Insufficient justification for design choices: why second-order finite difference for bumpiness? Why hinge penalty for uniformity? Why δ=0.2?
Limited statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or sensitivity analysis for hyperparameter selection (K=8, s=32/64)
